findings.title: Source of compiled Copilot content is unspecified, and the layout implies a Claude-artifact dependency
findings.description:
The file layout labels the sources as `.claude/rules/*.md` and `.claude/skills/*.md` (lines 42-43, 46-47). The slice never says whether the guide script's `copilot` backend reads these Claude-format files or the project-documents source rules. The stated driver is a user who cancelled their Claude subscription. For `cf init --ide copilot` on a fresh directory, the Claude-format artifacts may not exist unless `setup-ide claude` has run first. The slice plan describes "one-way source-of-truth → compiled target", not "Claude output → Copilot output".
- Name the input the copilot backend reads, and state that it works without a prior `cf setup-ide claude`.
- If it needs the Claude artifacts, say so as an explicit ordering dependency.
- Otherwise the plan's success criterion that `cf init --ide copilot` runs end-to-end on a fresh directory is not guaranteed.

findings.title: No failure-mode enumeration for the script step and the guide-sync coupling
findings.description:
The new I/O path is `execFileSync('bash', [scriptPath, 'copilot'])` followed by worktree copy. Only one failure is addressed, and only as an assertion: the Risks section (line 133) says a missing `copilot` case "will fail … with a clear error". Nothing in the design makes that true, and nothing says what an older guide script does with an unknown argument (non-zero exit versus silent success). Unaddressed failures:
- **Older guides:** the script runs but has no `copilot` case. Specify a fail-fast check or an exit-code contract, and an observable error.
- **Mid-run script failure:** the existing file was already backed up to `.bak` and the script dies partway. This leaves a half-compiled `.github/` tree. State whether this is acceptable, how the user recovers, and what is logged.
- **Hang:** `execFileSync` has no timeout.
- **Worktree propagation:** a source path such as `.github/prompts/` may not exist (no skills), and a worktree may be unreachable. Decide whether this skips with a warning or errors.

Each handling choice should be observable (WARNING+ log or error exit), and at least one test should assert the signal. The Test Coverage section (lines 121-129) has no failure-path case for the script step.

findings.title: Managed-marker safety check covers two files, but the script writes two whole directories
findings.description:
Step 4 checks only `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `AGENTS.md`. The script also writes `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` and `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`. A user's existing hand-written files there could be overwritten with no prompt or backup. The plan states the contract as "first-run warns before overwriting unmanaged user content", and the design only partly meets it. Related gaps:
- It does not say how stale generated files are handled when a source rule is removed.
- "prompt (or skip with `--yes`), backup" is ambiguous. It could mean skip the file or skip the prompt and overwrite with a backup.
- The helper name differs between sections: `isManagedCopilot(filePath)` (line 29) and `isManagedCopilotFiles(projectPath)` (line 109). Pick one and give it one signature.

findings.title: Translation requirements are narrowed from the plan and have no test coverage
findings.description:
The plan requires that the "translator must handle both forms" of the `paths` frontmatter (array and string). The slice describes only `paths: string[]` (line 32 and the `applyTo` section). The plan's success criterion "Path→applyTo translation correctly converts Claude frontmatter to Copilot frontmatter" has no matching test in Test Coverage (lines 121-129). Those tests cover only CF-core behavior. The translator, the highest-risk piece per the plan's "frontmatter translation correctness" risk, lives in the submodule and is untested in this design.
- Restore both-forms handling.
- Add translation tests that use real rule files from the project, per the project's parser-fixture rule.
- Cover the omitted-`paths` case, and the case where a rule with no `paths` is routed to `copilot-instructions.md` instead of being emitted as a split file.

findings.title: Plan-assigned deliverables are dropped without being recorded
findings.description: The plan says to "document the mapping" for `.claude/agents/*.md` → Copilot custom agents, and to reference the tool guide `project-documents/user/tool-guides/copilot-vscode/setup-ide.md`. The slice defers agents ("document the mapping but defer") but does not record the mapping. It also never references the tool guide, which is a plan success criterion. Either add the mapping row and the tool guide reference, or state explicitly that they are deferred.

findings.title: Per-target path knowledge is repeated in three places
findings.description: The Copilot path set (`AGENTS.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/instructions/`, `.github/prompts/`) appears in the managed-check, the propagation branch and the layout. The slice also says it "establishes the pattern" for future targets, but that pattern is an `else if (target === …)` chain. A single per-target table (managed files plus propagated paths) consumed by both the safety check and propagation would match the project's rule against scattered comparison values. It would also make the "add a new target" claim true at lower cost. This is not blocking.
